title: knapsack, subset-sum, and resource-allocation DP
concepts: Knapsack DP chooses items subject to a capacity or resource budget; the state records which items remain eligible and how much capacity is available.
In 0/1 knapsack each item may be selected once, so a one-dimensional capacity loop runs downward to avoid reusing the current item.
In unbounded knapsack an item may be reused, so a one-dimensional capacity loop commonly runs upward; loop order encodes the reuse rule.
Subset sum asks whether selected values reach a target and is a special boolean knapsack recurrence; reachable sums can be represented with a boolean array or bitset.
Partition equal subset sum first checks that the total is even, then asks whether a subset reaches half the total; this reduction should be proved before applying the DP.
Target-sum counting can map plus/minus assignments to a subset-sum count when parity and range conditions are satisfied.
The O(nW) dynamic program is pseudo-polynomial because it depends on numeric capacity W rather than the number of bits needed to encode W.
When reconstructing selected items, preserve predecessor choices or use a carefully justified recomputation; equal-value choices may produce multiple optimal subsets.
